Describe the arguments of rbiom functions.

Source: R/fn_schema.r
fn_schema.Rd

A machine-readable description of what each argument of an rbiom function accepts: its kind, its fixed choices, numeric limits, whether NULL is allowed and what it means, and where dataset-dependent choices come from. Another program (such as a web interface) can use it to draw input controls and to check a request without calling the function. The same description is what the functions use to check their own arguments, so the two cannot disagree.

Usage

fn_schema(fn = NULL, json = FALSE)

Arguments

fn

The name of a function, e.g. "adiv_boxplot". NULL describes every covered function. Default: NULL

json

Return the description as JSON text instead of an R list. Default: FALSE

Value

With fn, one entry (a list). Without, a named list of entries, one per covered function, so names(fn_schema()) lists the covered functions. With json = TRUE, the same as a JSON string.

Entries

Each entry has:

fn

The function's name.

returns

What the function returns: type is one of "plot", "table", "factor", "matrix", "dist", "biom", or "file"; has lists the $ fields the result carries (e.g. "data", "code", "stats").

counts

(Optional) The counts the function should be given, where it makes a difference: "rarefied" (diversity and abundance compared at one sequencing depth), or "unrarefied" (rarefaction curves, rarefy() itself, and differential abundance, which models sequencing depth itself).

needs

(Optional) An optional package the function requires.

rules

(Optional) Constraints between arguments, each one of: one_of (exactly one of these arguments must be non-NULL); any_of (at least one must be); or when (conditions, as for an argument's when) with requires (these arguments must then be non-NULL) or forbids (they must then be NULL).

params

One entry per argument, in the order of formals().

Arguments

Every argument has name, type, and desc (the first sentence of its help text). The other fields are present only when they apply.

type

One of: "logical", "integer", "number", "string"; "choice" (one or more of choices); "layers" (plot layers: choices lists each letter and name; letters may be run together, as in "xd"); "field" (metadata field names: see class); "rank" (taxonomic ranks of the dataset, by name or by position: 1 is the highest rank, -1 the lowest, 0 the OTUs); "taxa" (see forms); "metric" (div is "alpha" or "beta"; choices lists each metric's id, name, whether it is phylogenetic, needing a tree, and whether it needs integer counts, int_only); "aesthetic" (colors, shapes, or patterns: aes, and by, the argument whose values they are mapped to); "palette"; "tracks"; "biom", "tree", "dist", "vector", "file", "dots" (R objects, a file path, and ...: see r_only).

required

TRUE when the argument has no default.

default

The default value, from formals().

default_expr, default_note

For a default that is an expression, such as stat.by = x: the expression (not evaluated) and what it means. default is then NULL.

null

Present when NULL is accepted: what it means.

choices

The fixed options. Matching ignores case and accepts unambiguous abbreviations.

choices_needs

The choices that need an optional package, as choice = package (layer name = package for layers), e.g. tSNE = "Rtsne". Choices not listed need nothing extra.

choices_when

Options that depend on other arguments: a list of when conditions (as below) with the choices that apply while they hold. The first that holds applies; otherwise choices.

min, max

Numeric limits. "integer" values must be whole.

max_n

How many values may be given. Absent: any number.

per_side

One value for both rows and columns of a heat map, or two: for rows, then columns.

class

For fields: "categorical", "numeric", or "any".

coerce

For categorical fields: numeric fields are accepted too, and treated as categories.

ops

For fields: field names may be prefixed with "==" (compare within groups) or "!=" (between groups).

extra

For fields: values accepted besides the dataset's fields, such as ".taxa".

forms

The forms accepted, when there are several: "logical" (TRUE or FALSE); "true" (TRUE only); "integer"; "string"; "choice" (one of choices); "palette" (a palette name from list_palettes(), optionally prefixed with "-" to reverse it); "values" (a vector of colors, shapes, or patterns); "named_values" (a vector named by the values of by); "count" (the n most abundant taxa); "fraction" (a number below 1: taxa with at least that mean relative abundance); "names" (taxa names at the chosen rank); "fields" (metadata field names); "spec" (a list of options; see the function's help).

palettes

The palette kinds suited to the argument.

needs

An optional package the argument requires.

when

Conditions under which the argument has any effect; all must hold. Each names a param and one of: is (its value is one of these), is_not, has_any (it includes one of these), is_null, not_null. Values are canonical: layer names, not letters, and metric ids. Absent: the argument may always matter.

deprecated

The version that deprecated the argument.

r_only

Only an R caller can set it: an R object, a file path, a host setting such as cpus, or .... fn_check() refuses it.

note

Anything else a caller needs to know.

In JSON, NULL is null, numbers are written in full, Inf is the string "Inf", and the list fields (choices, forms, ops, palettes, has, and the values in when) are always arrays. choices_needs is an object.

The description is part of rbiom's interface: any change to it comes with a new package version, so a caller can cache it by packageVersion("rbiom"). The metric choices come from the installed version of the ecodive package.

See also

fn_check() to check arguments against a dataset; list_palettes() and list_metrics().

Examples

    library(rbiom)

    head(names(fn_schema()))
#> [1] "adiv_boxplot"  "adiv_corrplot" "adiv_stats"    "adiv_matrix"  
#> [5] "adiv_table"    "bdiv_boxplot" 

    x <- fn_schema("adiv_boxplot")
    x$returns
#> $type
#> [1] "plot"
#> 
#> $has
#> [1] "data"  "code"  "stats"
#> 
    str(x$params[[10]])
#> List of 6
#>  $ name   : chr "test"
#>  $ type   : chr "choice"
#>  $ choices: chr [1:5] "auto" "none" "wilcox" "emmeans" ...
#>  $ max_n  : num 1
#>  $ default: chr "auto"
#>  $ desc   : chr "Method for computing p-values."

    fn_schema("rarefy", json = TRUE)
#> {"fn":"rarefy","returns":{"type":"biom","has":["code"]},"counts":"unrarefied","params":[{"name":"biom","type":"biom","required":true,"r_only":true,"desc":"An rbiom object, or any value accepted by `as_rbiom()`."},{"name":"depth","type":"integer","min":1,"max_n":1,"null":"Chosen automatically, as by suggest_rarefy_depth().","default":null,"desc":"The number of observations to keep per sample."},{"name":"seed","type":"integer","min":0,"max_n":1,"default":0,"desc":"Random seed for selecting which observations to keep."},{"name":"inflate","type":"logical","max_n":1,"default":false,"desc":"Logical. Handling for non-integer data (e.g. relative abundances)."},{"name":"clone","type":"logical","r_only":true,"max_n":1,"default":true,"desc":"Create a copy of `biom` before modifying."},{"name":"cpus","type":"integer","r_only":true,"min":1,"max":256,"max_n":1,"null":"All available cores.","default":null,"default_expr":"n_cpus()","default_note":"All available cores.","desc":"The number of CPUs to use."}]}
